title: The Second Voyage of HMS Beagle
intro: HMS Beagle left Plymouth on 27 December 1831 on a survey expedition under Robert FitzRoy, who had sought a naturalist to investigate geology. Charles Darwin, aged 22, accepted the place. The ship surveyed the coasts of southern South America and returned by Tahiti and Australia, circling the Earth.
ending: Beagle reached Falmouth on 2 October 1836. The voyage had been offered to Darwin as a two-year trip and lasted almost five years. Darwin spent most of it exploring on land, and his journal later made him widely known as a writer.

legs.title: Across the Atlantic to the Río de la Plata

stops.text: After delays from westerly gales, Beagle left its anchorage in the Barn Pool on the morning of 27 December 1831 and set out on its surveying expedition.
stops.quote: Finally, on the morning of 27 December, Beagle left its anchorage in the Barn Pool, under Mount Edgecumbe on the west side of Plymouth Sound and set out on its surveying expedition.

stops.text: Beagle reached Tenerife in the Canary Islands but was quarantined because of cholera in England. Darwin was denied a landing, to his intense disappointment, and the ship sailed on.
stops.quote: Then on 6 January, it reached Tenerife in the Canary Islands but was quarantined there because of cholera in England.

stops.text: Beagle made its first landing at Praia on Santiago in the Cape Verde Islands. FitzRoy set up an observatory on Quail Island, and Darwin studied its geology and first thought of writing a book on the subject.
stops.quote: Six days later, they made their first landing at Praia on the volcanic island of Santiago in the Cape Verde Islands.

stops.text: Beagle reached the port of Bahia in Brazil to rate the chronometers and take on water. Darwin found slavery offensive, and when he doubted FitzRoy's account of slaves' answers to their master, FitzRoy banned him from his company, then apologised within hours.
stops.quote: then FitzRoy pressed on to Bahia de Todos Santos, Brazil, to rate the chronometers and take on water. They reached the continent and arrived at the port on 28 February.

stops.text: Beagle entered Rio de Janeiro harbour, where FitzRoy took longitude observations from Villegagnon Island. Darwin took lodgings at Botafogo and set off with local estate owners on a riding excursion to Rio Macaé.
stops.quote: They manoeuvred Beagle into Rio de Janeiro harbour "in first rate style" on 4 April, with Darwin enthusiastically helping.

stops.text: During a cruise round Bahía Blanca, Darwin and FitzRoy stopped at Punta Alta. In the low cliffs Darwin found fossilised teeth and bones of gigantic extinct mammals and collected them over several days.
stops.quote: on 22 September, and about ten miles (16 km) from the ship, they stopped for a while at Punta Alta. In low cliffs near the point, Darwin found conglomerate rocks containing numerous shells and fossilised teeth and bones of gigantic extinct mammals

stops.text: Beagle reached Tierra del Fuego with the three Fuegians taken to England on the earlier voyage. Darwin met the Yaghan people for the first time and judged them harshly, in terms he later used in The Descent of Man.
stops.quote: They reached Tierra del Fuego on 18 December 1832, and Darwin was taken by surprise at what he perceived as the crude savagery of the Yaghan natives

stops.text: Exploring the geology of the cliffs near the harbour, Darwin found pieces of a spine and a hind leg. He took them for a large animal such as a mastodon; Richard Owen later named the creature Macrauchenia.
stops.quote: On 9 January 1834, 110 miles (180 km) further south, they reached Port St Julian and exploring the local geology in cliffs near the harbour Darwin found fossils of pieces of spine and a hind leg of

stops.place: Tierra del Fuego, the mission site
stops.text: Beagle returned to visit the missionaries and found their huts deserted. Jemmy Button, one of the three Fuegians, came out in a canoe, having lost his possessions and settled into the native ways with a wife.
stops.quote: After further surveying in Tierra del Fuego, they returned on 5 March 1834 to visit the missionaries but found the huts deserted.

stops.text: An expedition including FitzRoy and Darwin took boats up the Santa Cruz river, with everyone taking turns hauling them upstream. Darwin read the terraces of shingle as old shores that had gradually risen. They turned back near the Andes.
stops.quote: Beagle now sailed to southern Patagonia, and on 19 April, an expedition including FitzRoy and Darwin set off to take boats as far as possible up the Santa Cruz river

legs.title: The west coast of South America

stops.text: Beagle and Adventure reached Chiloé in the wet, heavily wooded archipelago and then spent six months surveying the coast and islands southwards. Darwin found fragments of black lignite and petrified wood there.
stops.quote: reaching Chiloé Island in the wet and heavily wooded Chiloé Archipelago on 28 June 1834.

stops.text: Beagle arrived at Valparaíso. Darwin set off up the volcanic Andes on 14 August with a companion, then fell ill on his way back from Santiago and spent a month in bed.
stops.quote: They arrived at Valparaíso on 23 July,

stops.text: Twelve days after arriving, Darwin was on shore when a severe earthquake struck. He returned to find the port town badly damaged.
stops.quote: They arrived at the port of Valdivia on 8 February 1835. Twelve days later, Darwin was on shore when he experienced a severe earthquake and returned to find the port town badly damaged.

stops.text: Beagle found Concepción devastated by the same earthquake and a tsunami. FitzRoy found mussel beds now above high tide, evidence that the ground had risen about 9 feet.
stops.quote: They sailed two hundred miles (320 km) north to Concepción, and arrived on 4 March to find that the same earthquake had devastated the city by repeated shocks and a tsunami, with even the cathedral in ruins.

stops.text: Beagle sailed to Lima, where an armed insurrection kept Darwin with the ship. While writing up his notes he reached the idea that coral atolls formed as volcanic islands sank. FitzRoy joined them on 9 September.
stops.quote: On 9 September Blonde brought FitzRoy to join them at Lima.

stops.text: Beagle anchored at Chatham Island in the Galápagos. Darwin spent his first hour ashore at what is now called Frigatebird Hill and began to collect plants, reptiles, birds and insects across the islands.
stops.quote: A week out of Lima, Beagle reached the Galápagos Islands on 15 September 1835. The next day Captain FitzRoy dropped anchor near where the town of Puerto Baquerizo Moreno is now sited, at Chatham Island.

stops.text: Beagle reached Tahiti, where Darwin found the vegetation luxuriant and the people pleasant and intelligent. He thought they showed the benefits of Christianity and doubted what he had read about tyrannical missionaries.
stops.quote: Arriving at Tahiti on 15 November, he soon found interest in luxuriant vegetation and the pleasant intelligent natives who showed the benefits of Christianity

stops.text: Darwin first sighted Australia on 12 January 1836 and admired Sydney. Inland he met Aboriginal people who gave a spear-throwing display for a shilling, and he reflected sadly that their numbers were falling.
stops.quote: The first sight of Australia on 12 January 1836 reminded him of Patagonia, but inland the country improved, and he was soon filled with admiration at the bustling city of Sydney.

stops.text: At Hobart, Darwin noted that the Aboriginal people of Tasmania had been removed and kept in effect as prisoners on a promontory. He wrote that the settlers' misconduct had first led to this step.
stops.quote: Beagle visited Hobart, Tasmania, where Darwin was impressed by the agreeable high society of the settlers but noted that the island's "Aboriginal blacks are all removed & kept (in reality as prisoners) in a Promontory, the neck of which is guarded.

stops.text: The Admiralty had asked for a survey of a coral atoll. On arrival the whole crew set to work, and FitzRoy's soundings supported Darwin's theory that encircling reefs become atolls as an island sinks.
stops.quote: He chose the Keeling Islands in the Indian Ocean, and on arrival on 1 April, the entire crew set to work.

stops.text: At the Cape, Darwin learned that extracts from his letters to Henslow had been printed as a pamphlet. Around 15 June he and FitzRoy visited the astronomer Sir John Herschel.
stops.quote: Beagle reached the Cape of Good Hope on 31 May.

stops.text: Beagle stopped on St Helena for six days. Darwin lodged near Napoleon's tomb, studied the island's strata and volcanic dykes, and noted that goats and hogs introduced in 1502 had destroyed much of the woodland.
stops.quote: On 8 July, they stopped at St. Helena for six days.

stops.text: At Ascension Darwin received letters from his sisters telling him of Sedgwick's praise for the collection he had sent home. He also climbed over the volcanic rocks with his geological hammer.
stops.quote: Beagle reached Ascension Island on 19 July 1836, and Darwin was delighted to receive letters from his sisters

stops.text: After a stormy passage with a stop at the Azores, Beagle anchored at Falmouth. Darwin left that night by the Royal Mail coach and reached his family home at Shrewsbury late on 4 October.
stops.quote: After a stormy passage including a stop for supplies at the Azores, the Beagle finally reached England on 2 October 1836 and anchored at Falmouth, Cornwall.

notes: Years of 1832 for Tenerife, Praia, Bahia, Rio and Punta Alta, and 1834 for Valparaíso, are supplied from the voyage's order; the article gives only day and month there. Praia has no day (the article says 'Six days later' after 10 or 11 January). Hobart has no date in the article; 1836 follows from its order. Tierra del Fuego is used for two stops and the mission post at 'Buttons Land' (23 January 1833) is left out; the wp title is the island, a large area. The entry 'praia' is assumed to be Praia in Cape Verde (the places.tsv gives only the name). Left out for the 24-stop limit: St Paul's Rocks, Montevideo, Port Desire, the Strait of Magellan, the Falkland Islands, Copiapó, Tagus Cove, New Zealand (a country, no town named), Mauritius, the second visit to Bahia and Pernambuco. The article says Darwin's Falmouth to Shrewsbury trip was a two-day journey. The article's description of Darwin's views on Yaghan, Māori and Aboriginal peoples is his own, and the texts give only what he noted. The wp titles 'Puerto San Julián', 'Punta Alta', 'Santa Cruz River (Argentina)' and 'San Cristóbal Island' are my best guesses at the Wikipedia titles and should be checked.
